sealed.statement: Desired replication factor has a policy authority that is independent of replica identities: it comes only from a valid persisted policy row for the owning table, creation initializes that policy from the owning table's schema declaration, runtime identity mutation cannot change a declared policy, and an identity count is never persisted as desired RF. A minted replace-replica-<hex> is a new identity, not a changed factor. This Quest establishes the substrate ONLY; it does not claim that every behaviour-changing consumer already resolves through it.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

Exactly one module decodes a persisted policy row into a desired replication factor, returning a frozen {replicationFactor, source} projection and nothing else; it mints no runtime state, reads only own data properties, never executes an accessor on a candidate row, and rejects arrays, inherited values, non-integers, coercible strings and non-positive values as UNDECLARED with factor 0.

The creation default for each table is READ from that table's own schema declaration, so PARTITIONS rows follow the PARTITIONS declaration and MESSAGE_GROUPS rows follow the MESSAGE_GROUPS declaration; the schema default seeds a NEW row and is never used to reinterpret a row that failed to declare a usable value.

No code path derives, writes, or persists a desired replication factor from a replica identity list: getInitialReplicaIds hands out a copy, PartitionService and MessageGroupService copy the peer list they are given, seed hand-offs do not alias the declaration, and no identity count such as replicas.length is written into a policy field.

This Quest proves the substrate only. It makes NO claim that every behaviour-changing desired-RF consumer resolves through the authority, states no consumer inventory, and does not repair the known move-planner table-policy fallback; those belong to the successor quest behaviour-changing-consumer-convergence and to S6.

Proof is a deterministic raw node:test witness with one anchored scenario per receipt, red on HEAD and green after, with a from-scratch mutation matrix in which every mutation of the substrate reds at least one named receipt.

claim: The bootstrap-membership lane carries two PRE-EXISTING marginal integration failures, both reproduced on clean HEAD 3cddfcf65 and neither caused by this candidate. (1) node-join-convergence-slo assertion 7 'over-target voter duration should stay bounded' failed on clean HEAD at 6340ms <= 2000ms and on the candidate at 2226ms <= 2000ms — the candidate's measured value is roughly three times CLOSER to the bound, so the authority change does not widen the over-target window. This assertion is measured against desired RF and is therefore directly relevant to S6a: over-target voters are a placement-convergence signal and the bound is marginal on HEAD today. (2) seed-owner-read-diagnosis times out only under thermal throttling; it completes in 31.1-31.7s on baseline and 29.5-30.2s on the candidate against a ~32s budget, so the candidate is not slower and the margin is thin on HEAD. Candidate lane on a cooled machine: 244/245 with only the pre-existing SLO assertion red; storage-partition 141/141.

claim: RETRACTION of the immediately preceding finding with kind 'zzz' and claim 'probe for valid kinds'. That entry is not a finding: it was an accidental CLI probe of which --kind values are accepted, and it revealed that solve finding accepts an arbitrary unvalidated kind string rather than rejecting an unknown one. Independent verifier REJECTED review-f13d7333ce1c4a55cca51e37 with five BLOCKING findings, four of them new mutations that left the sealed 13-receipt bar fully green. (1) creation-default-per-owning-schema violated IN BAR: seed-registration-phase.js still persisted replica_count from BOOTSTRAP_MESSAGE_GROUP.REPLICA_COUNT, a restated literal 3 agreeing with MESSAGE_GROUPS_SCHEMA only by coincidence, 250 lines from a hunk the candidate edited. (2) Mutation A re-pointed the PRODUCTION message-group creation write at the PARTITIONS authority - the exact cross-table leak this quest claims to close - and stayed 13/13 green: the two arrows pinned only the module constants, never which constant the SITE consumes, and 3 == 3 defeated the comparison. (3) Mutation B set the PARTITIONS creation write to literal 1 and stayed green; that half of the creation claim had NO witness. (4) Mutation C: node --test --test-name-pattern exits 0 on zero matches and prints tests 1 / pass 1 for the file-level subtest, so a renamed scenario passed and EVERY receipt was a shell proving only that the file loaded. (5) every-critical-table-declares-the-same-target was vacuous - it built each row from the default and asserted 3 == 3, reading no per-table declaration. Non-blocking: the spelling loop rescued a rejected snake value via the camel alias; safe-integer, camel-alias acceptance and unsafe integers were unwitnessed; two prose overreaches; a Proxy can forge a factor and execute a trap. The verifier confirmed identity isolation is real on the production PartitionService and MessageGroupService paths, no decoder-or-raw re-read exists, no consumer-inventory claim appears anywhere, and the control mutation reds exactly one receipt. All five blocking items are repaired; the fingerprint no longer matches the sealed review because the repair changed the candidate, so a fresh review id must carry the re-verification.

Third pre-existing marginal integration failure, reproduced on clean HEAD 3cddfcf65: managed-split-admission-reliability.integration.test.js times out at ~32s ('managed split persists blocked split admission instead of generic failure', 21 of 31 assertions reached). Clean HEAD failed 2 of 4 isolated runs; the candidate failed 1 of 3. It shares an exact signature with the other two known flakes (seed-owner-read-diagnosis and node-join-convergence-slo assertion 4): a test-level budget of about 32 seconds that the run completes just under when the machine is cool and crosses when it is not, with the assertion count truncating rather than an assertion failing. Final candidate lane results: bootstrap-membership 244/245 with only seed-owner-read-diagnosis red at 32.7s, storage-partition 141/141 on the first run and 140/141 on the second with only this test red. This is a HEAD-level test-budget fragility affecting at least three convergence integration tests, worth its own quest; it is not caused by and not repaired by this candidate.

claim: A SECOND policy authority survives inside the same seeded message_groups row, and is deliberately NOT repaired here. The row's replica_count now reads MESSAGE_GROUPS_SCHEMA, but the same row's policy column is JSON.stringify(BOOTSTRAP_MESSAGE_GROUP.POLICY), which still carries TARGET_REPLICA_COUNT: 3 as a restated literal in the same frozen object whose REPLICA_COUNT key this candidate deleted. So one row carries a schema-derived declared replica_count and a literal placement target that agree only by coincidence, exactly the divergence shape already recorded for move-planner.js line 281. This is the placement-target authority, which the epic transfers to S6 after S6a's causal measurement, so repairing it here would pre-empt that decision and widen this substrate quest past its declared scope. Also out of bar and recorded for the successor: table-creation-service writes partitions.replica_count from the config-driven service.defaultReplicaCount, a third creation-default authority the substrate does not cover.

Round-2 verifier REJECTED review-04d797f8d8245bb764c76b5f with two blocking findings, and confirmed all five round-1 repairs are real and not special-cased (it replayed each round-1 mutation, attacked the anchored runner five further ways - a forged top-level ok line on stdout, a skipped test, a nested subtest with the target name, a name that extends the target, and regex metacharacters - and found each correctly rejected). BLOCKING 1: an identity count could re-enter persisted policy through a MAXIMUM. Math.max(DECLARED_MESSAGE_GROUP_REPLICA_COUNT_DEFAULT, replicas.length) left 16/16 green and persisted replica_count 5, because the receipt drove the creation path with a SINGLE replica, so assert.notEqual compared 3 against 1 and was trivially true. The probe now supplies FIVE local replicas, more than the declared default, and asserts that precondition explicitly. BLOCKING 2: harness self-trust circularity. Neutering the anchored runner so it always reports success left the harness at 16/16 while node --test on the witness reported a real failure - the round-1 shell-receipt defect moved one level up, since the harness-fidelity control was itself executed by the component it validates. The control's receipt command now inverts the runner directly in the shell: if the runner ACCEPTS a scenario that does not exist, the receipt fails regardless of what it reports. Non-blocking also repaired: the typed source STRINGS are pinned (renaming them left 16/16 green); the three remaining seed hand-offs are converted so every declaration read goes through getInitialReplicaIds; the classifier is now asserted as a unit from the witness; and three prose overreaches are corrected, including the authority-mints receipt which now states that internal memoisation is NOT distinguished. Recorded and deliberately not repaired: BOOTSTRAP_MESSAGE_GROUP.POLICY.TARGET_REPLICA_COUNT remains a restated literal 3 serialized into the same seeded row - the placement-target authority, transferred to S6.

Round-3 verifier REJECTED review-255e883b76e79ff8024f7210 with three blocking findings, and the diagnosis was that BOTH round-2 repairs were special-cased against the exact mutation that exposed them rather than establishing a general property. (1) The harness-fidelity control guarded only the ABSENT case, so a runner that accepts a FAILING scenario satisfied it: rewriting classifyRun so any top-level result line counts as passed left the harness at 16/16 while node --test on the witness reported a real failure. A runner short-circuited to answer by probe NAME also stayed green, because the control used one fixed literal probe. (2) The identity-count repair only moved a threshold: Math.max(DECLARED, replicas.length - 2) passed both data points because the in-process probe and the drift probe varied the declaration AND the count together, so any offset maximum slipped through while production would still derive policy from identities. (3) Neither seed-registration write was protected, and the churn arrow lengthened a single identity list, so a CROSS-table identity length reaching partitions.replica_count was invisible. Repairs are now general properties, not point fixes: the control drives a fixture file covering all three outcome classes (passed, failed, absent) and demands the runner's verdict on each, so a runner wrong in ANY direction or keyed to a name fails; persisted policy is asserted INVARIANT across six identity counts straddling the declared default; the churn arrow lengthens EVERY identity list including the message-group one and both seed writes are inspected, split by owning table; and the accepted spelling set is pinned in the widening direction, since prepending target_replica_count had left the bar green and that key already exists in this codebase. Matrix rebuilt from scratch: 27 mutations, all red, including all five of this round's.

Round-4 verifier REJECTED review-7af02330a2aea792c035446e: six new mutations, all left 16/16 green, four blocking. The diagnosis across four rounds is now the decisive fact: the sealed clause 'an identity count is never persisted as desired RF' is UNIVERSAL, and I was chasing it with SAMPLES. Each round ruled out the variants someone thought to try - a maximum, then an offset maximum, then a ternary on nodeId - while the next round found another. Round 4's survivors were: a runner honest only for the fixture path (suppressing its own detector while three witness scenarios were red); offset maxima at BOTH seed-registration writes, which were still sampled at only two identity lengths; a node id reaching policy at the best-probed site, because every probe used nodeId 'seed'; an options.replicaIds.length branch inside the decoder itself, since no scenario constrained the decoder's accepted INPUT surface; and a spelling set guarded by a blocklist of eight guessed names, defeated by a ninth. The repair is structural rather than another sample. Three universals now hold: (1) in the creation-site files, EVERY persisted replica_count write must be a bare declared-default Identifier - any call, member access, ternary, arithmetic or literal fails whatever it evaluates to - with the known write count pinned so a moved write cannot make the check vacuous; (2) resolveDesiredReplicationFactor may read ONLY partitionRow from its options, asserted over the AST of its own body; (3) the accepted spelling set is read out of the module and compared whole as an allowlist. The harness-fidelity control additionally runs the witness file directly with the runner out of the mediating position, so no file-scoped cheat can suppress its detector. Matrix rebuilt from scratch: 33 mutations, all red, including all six of this round's.

Sealed-constraint wording note, recorded rather than edited because constraints are sealed and hand-editing a sealed bar is forbidden. The opening sentence of constraint single-policy-decoder ('Exactly one module decodes a persisted policy row into a desired replication factor') reads like a repo-wide inventory claim, while at least four other modules still decode partitionRow.replica_count directly. Those modules are the successor quest's scope and the sealed STATEMENT scopes this quest to the substrate, so the constraint is not false as scoped - but the successor quest should restate it unambiguously as 'exactly one module is the AUTHORITY that behaviour-changing readers resolve through', so the inventory claim lives only where it is proved. Also recorded: the structural persisted-write check is deliberately OVER-strict - it rejects a benign 'const X = DECLARED_DEFAULT; replica_count: X' alias. That is an accepted trade: the check is a proof anchor, and admitting one level of aliasing would admit arbitrary indirection, which is exactly how the earlier syntactic checks were defeated.

Round-5 verifier REJECTED review-c12fa95158dfc5b3552902db on TWO receipts, while confirming the shipped source is correct and minimal with no functional regression, that structural universal 1 holds as a set, that harness fidelity is materially repaired (the round-4 fixture-path bypass now reds because the control runs node --test on the witness directly, with the runner out of the mediating position), and that no consumer-inventory over-claim exists. The two blocking findings were both cases where a SYNTACTIC universal was narrower than it looked, each defeated in one ordinary refactoring step rather than by probe-aware code. (1) The decoder input-surface check walked only MemberExpression nodes whose object is the decoder's own options identifier, so a module helper taking the options object and reading candidateOptions.observedReplicas passed the check while resolveDesiredReplicationFactor returned 7 for a row declaring 3 plus a four-element identity list - identities authorizing policy inside the named authority module, exactly what constraint identities-never-authorize-policy forbids. (2) The spelling allowlist read the array literal out of the module source, so widening by spread from another frozen constant left that literal byte-identical while a forged spelling decoded to factor 99 with source partition_row_replica_count. In both cases the receipt's own stated claim was demonstrably false while the receipt was green, which is a false receipt rather than a weak one. The repair, which the verifier identified and I adopted, ends the regress by OBSERVING THE READS AT RUNTIME instead of inspecting syntax: a recording proxy passed as options records exactly partitionRow, and a recording proxy row records exactly the two probed spellings. Runtime observation cannot be dodged by a helper, alias, destructure, computed access, spread, concat, second lookup path, or pre-normalisation. Both strengthenings landed inside existing receipt ids, so the exhausted amendment budget was not an obstacle. Matrix rebuilt from scratch: 36 mutations, all red, including both round-5 blockers and the round-5 runner bypass.

mechanism: The sealed clauses are UNIVERSAL quantifications - no runtime quantity ever reaches persisted policy, the decoder reads only a policy row, exactly two spellings are accepted - but each proof attempt was an EXISTENTIAL enumeration. A sampled proof rules out only the variants someone thought of, so round after round the next unenumerated variant (maximum, offset maximum, node-id ternary, config read) passed. Replacing samples with AST assertions moved the failure rather than removing it: a syntactic universal quantifies over the SYNTAX it can see, so one level of ordinary indirection - a helper taking the options object, a spread from another frozen constant - satisfies the check while the claim is false. Five rejections are one observation defect, not five source defects.
intervention: Prove read-surface claims by OBSERVING the reads at runtime: pass a recording Proxy as the decoder options and as the candidate policy row, and assert the exact set of keys actually probed. The observation sits at the real boundary the claim is about, so it is invariant under how the code reaches that boundary.
expectedMovement: Mutations that route a runtime quantity into policy through NEW indirection - helper functions, aliases, destructuring, computed access, spread, concat, a second lookup path, pre-normalisation - red without the witness naming that indirection.
negativeResultMeans: If a runtime-observed proof still admits a green mutation that changes production behaviour, the technique is not the cure and the receipt STRUCTURE is at fault, which means this quest must be parked and a successor authored with a receipt set designed around observed boundaries from the start.
discriminator: A mutation using an indirection the witness never mentions must red. The two round-5 blockers are exactly this shape: a module helper reading candidateOptions.observedReplicas, and REPLICA_COUNT_COLUMNS widened by spread with the array literal byte-identical. Both were green under the syntactic proof and both must red under the runtime one.

modelGuidance.instruction: Use this gate as the Quest theory discriminator for architecture, owner-boundary, core-system, lifecycle, or model-contract theories. At the model rung, pass the modelRef unless a finding explains why the architecture model is not applicable.

promotionRule: Both round-5 blockers red, the full matrix stays red, and an independent verifier finds no new indirection route: adopt runtime observation as the standard technique for read-surface claims and carry it into successor quest B.
rejectionRule: Any indirection-based mutation still leaves the bar green: reject the technique, park this frontier, and author the successor closure rather than attempting a seventh round.

claim: Round-6 verifier REJECTED review-87daed131cbb5502eaa64b11 and classified the rejection explicitly: this is the RECEIPT-STRUCTURE case, not the shipped-source case. The candidate module is correct and minimal as written today; no production behaviour is false. The attack that lands is that each recording Proxy observes exactly ONE execution path. The options proxy is passed with a row declaring 3, so only the DECLARED branch is recorded; the row proxy declares nothing, so only the UNDECLARED branch is recorded. The complementary branch is unobserved in each case. Five new mutations, none in the existing 36, all left the witness at 16 pass 0 fail: an identity fallback taken only when declared === null (a row with no replica_count plus seven identities returns factor 7 - the single most natural drift in this module, and a violation of both identities-never-authorize-policy and the fail-closed clause); probing target_replica_count only AFTER a valid replica_count is found (factor 99, using the very forge surface the receipt names); reading Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(options, 'peers'), since the options proxy has no gOPD trap; reading this.replicaIds, since every scenario calls the decoder bare; and caching options at module level so one caller's identity list sets another caller's factor. Controls confirmed the round-5 repair is real but narrow: both round-5 blockers and a plain-object normalisation now red. The verifier's conclusion, which I accept, is that runtime observation quantifies over the paths and object channels the witness happens to exercise - the same existential shape that lost in rounds 1-4 as behavioural sampling and in round 5 as syntactic universals. Closing these five needs five different point repairs, not one closure, so the regress continues. Regression checks held: exactly three persisted writes, all bare declared-default identifiers with the count pinned; the harness-fidelity control still runs node --test on the witness directly; no consumer-inventory over-claim anywhere.

note: Six independent reviews, six rejections, and the sixth classified it explicitly: the SHIPPED SOURCE is correct and minimal, and the receipt STRUCTURE is what cannot carry the sealed claim. Two of A's clauses are universals about what code MAY DO - no runtime quantity is ever persisted as desired RF, and the decoder reads only a policy row. One of them, the persisted-write form, was provable and IS proved structurally over the AST with the write count pinned. The other is a purity/dataflow property of a module, and three successive techniques failed on it in the same shape: behavioural sampling covers the values someone thought of, syntactic universals cover the syntax they can see, and an instrumented invocation covers the paths and object channels that one call exercises. Each was defeated by the first channel it did not cover: a maximum, then a helper indirection, then a declared === null branch and a this-read. Proving it properly needs a module-level property - an isolated realm with an instrumented global plus a no-module-mutable-state check, or a dataflow analysis - which is verification INFRASTRUCTURE and is not proportionate to carry inside a substrate quest whose amendment budget is already exhausted at 2/2. The honest split is therefore between what the substrate proves and what a separate proof-technique quest must establish. Parking per the selected theory's own rejectionRule rather than attempting a seventh round.

claim: SUPERSEDED by operator decision on the recorded Round-6 result. The Round-6 verifier classified the rejection explicitly as the RECEIPT-STRUCTURE case: the shipped source is CORRECT and MINIMAL, no production behaviour is false, and the frontier metric is SOLVED. What cannot be discharged is the sealed clause 'the decoder reads only a policy row', which is a whole-program purity/dataflow assertion over JavaScript. In JavaScript an adversary can always introduce another channel through a helper, module state, this, a global or a closure, so discharging that universal requires an isolated realm with an instrumented global plus a no-module-mutable-state check, or a real dataflow analysis. That is verification INFRASTRUCTURE, it is not proportionate inside this quest, and chasing it converted the release proof into a general program-analysis problem across six rounds. The product invariant 0.2 actually needs is narrower and falsifiable: for a FIXED authoritative persisted policy row, runtime replica/identity state cannot change desired RF. The successor quest replication-target-authority-a2-contract replaces the over-strong universal with that observable authority-invariance contract, makes the boundary structural first by narrowing the decoder API to a positional persisted policy row, and proves the invariance metamorphically rather than by enumerating malicious expressions. No seventh adversarial round is run against the superseded universal. The whole-program purity claim is recorded as a verification-infrastructure research item and is NOT a prerequisite for B, S3 or S6.
